en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Earth.

10. The Question on the Requisites of a Wheel-Turning Monarch “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that four requisites of a wheel-turning monarch (cakkavatti) should be adopted—what are those four requisites that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a wheel-turning monarch wins over the people by means of the four bases of sympathy (saṅgahavatthu);”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should gather the minds of the four assemblies, support them, and gladden them.
This, Great King, is the first quality of a wheel-turning monarch that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, in the realm of a wheel-turning monarch, thieves do not arise.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi who is a practitioner of yoga should not give rise to thoughts of sensual desire, ill will, or cruelty.
This, Great King, is the second quality to be adopted from a wheel-turning monarch.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods:
"He who delights in the stilling of thoughts,
who constantly cultivates the perception of foulness while being mindful—
verily, he shall make an end."
"He understands this, having cut through the bonds of Māra.
Furthermore, Great King, just as a wheel-turning monarch travels day after day across the great earth bounded by the ocean, investigating both good and evil deeds;
even so, Great King, a practitioner devoted to yoga must daily review his bodily action, verbal action, and mental action, thinking: "Have I passed this day free from fault in these three respects?"
This, great king, is the third quality of a wheel-turning monarch that should be adopted.
And this was said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the noble Aṅguttara Nikāya:
“‘How are my days and nights passing?’—this is what one who has gone forth should frequently reflect upon.”
Furthermore, Great King, the internal and external protection of a wheel-turning monarch is well-arranged;
even so, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must station mindfulness as a gatekeeper for the protection against internal and external defilements.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality to be adopted from the wheel-turning monarch.
“Great King, this was also said by the Blessed One, the God above gods:

‘Monks, the noble disciple who has mindfulness as his gatekeeper abandons the unwholesome and develops the wholesome; he abandons what is blameworthy and develops what is blameless; he preserves himself in purity.
This is the tenth question, on the factors of a Wheel-turning Monarch.
The third chapter: The Earth Section (Pathavīvagga).
Its summary verse (uddāna) is:
Earth, water, and fire...
Vāyu and Pabbata;
Ākāsa and Candimasūriya;
Sakka and Cakkavatti.
